The trigger field.none: Only a person looking at the window can see what the trigger field shows. No test opens a window, so none reaches the owner's display. The value it shows comes from ConfigDocument::raw_trigger, which Rust tests in torpedo-core cover.

The alias list.none: Only a person looking at the window can see the alias rows. No test opens a window. The rows come from ConfigDocument::raw_aliases, which Rust tests cover.

Add, change and delete an alias.none: Only a person using the window can add, change and delete rows. No test opens a window. Each step saves through ConfigDocument::with_values and save, which the scenarios under Saving refuses a bad value and Saving keeps what the window does not manage show through the same torpedo-core functions.

A bad trigger in the window.none: Only a person looking at the window can see where the problem shows. No test opens a window. The check is check_values in torpedo-settings, which a Rust test covers, and the rule is config-file's The trigger value.

A bad value is not written.none: Only a person using the window can apply a field. No test opens a window. That nothing is written while a value is bad is check_values plus save, which Rust tests cover, and Saving a bad alias shows the same refusal through the mode without a window.

The skin tone selector.none: Only a person using the window can pick a tone in the selector. No test opens a window, so none reaches the owner's display. The pick saves through ConfigDocument::with_values and save, which Rust tests cover, and Set the skin tone shows the same save through --set-skin-tone. The labels come from tone_label, which a Rust test in torpedo-settings covers.

The usage switch.none: Only a person using the window can flip the switch. No test opens a window. The flip saves through ConfigDocument::with_values and save, which Rust tests cover, and Turn usage off shows the same save through --set-remember-usage.

Clear usage confirmed.none: Only a person using the window can answer the AdwAlertDialog. No test opens a window. The confirmed response deletes the usage file as --clear-usage does, which Clear the usage shows.

Clear usage cancelled.none: Only a person using the window can cancel the AdwAlertDialog. No test opens a window. The window connects the delete to the clear response only, so a cancel runs no code that touches the usage file.
